conventions.convention: The sector index set is finite and nonempty; every logical and ancillary space is nonzero and finite-dimensional. Distinct direct-sum sectors are orthogonal.

Both sector probability vectors are strictly positive and normalized. Ancillary density matrices are faithful and identical in the encoded state and reference; logical reference matrices are faithful, while logical state matrices may be singular.
Entropy uses natural logarithms and is measured in nats. Zero eigenvalues contribute zero through the convention 0 log 0 := 0; spectral logarithms themselves are taken on positive eigenvalues.
The identities concern finite matrices and do not identify ancillary entropy with geometric area or establish a gravitational entropy formula.
The second ancillary dimension is an integer d ≥ 1; d = 1 is included and gives zero ancillary entropy.

load_bearing.statement: For finite nonempty I and nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces Hα,Kα, define Eχ(p,ρ) = ⊕α pα ρα ⊗ χα, with strictly positive normalized p and fixed faithful ancillary density matrices χα.

Under the stated finite-sector hypotheses, ρA and σA are density matrices, σA is faithful, s(ρA) = H(p) + Σα pα(s(ρα) + s(χα)), and D(ρA‖σA) = Dcl(p‖q) + Σα pα D(ρα‖σα). These are exact finite-dimensional matrix identities.

seams_checked.note: Opened prop-tgrx-finite-modular-balance and its cited suppliers. The sector proposition's F1 preserves the finite-dimensional, normalized-state and faithful-reference hypotheses. Its proof establishes encoded-reference faithfulness before applying the identity globally and sectorwise.

The dictionary postulate uses the finite identity as a formulation prerequisite. Its Remarks explicitly distinguish conversion from nats by kB from any identification with geometric area, and its minimum rule remains an adopted physical premise.

The fusion-count and projector propositions faithfully reuse the density-matrix and spectral-entropy definitions. They establish normalization before calculating log dimension or log rank, and retain the distinction between diagrammatic closure trace and ordinary Hilbert-space trace. The fusion transition diagram agrees with the displayed matrix convention.
